examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Non-Pivot Columns of a Matrix in Row Echelon Form
examples.problem:
The row echelon form matrix $C$ is given below. What are its **non**-pivot columns?

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$
examples.worked_solution:
Remember that the pivots of a matrix in row echelon form are the first non-zero entries in each row of the matrix.

We can see that $C$ has $3$ pivots in the $1$st, $3$rd, and $4$th columns:

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Therefore, the only non-pivot column is the $2$nd column.

feedback.problem:
The row echelon form matrix $M$ is given below. What are the pivot columns of $M?$

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 4 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 7 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
Remember that the pivots of a matrix in row echelon form are the first non-zero entries in each row of the matrix.

We can see that $M$ has $3$ pivots in the $1$st, $2$nd, and $3$rd columns:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 4 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 7 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$
